headline: I Am The College Intern Who Accidentally Filled The Prime Minister’s Water Glass To The Brim Before His Iconic Speech
body:
When I saw the news that the Prime Minister was returning to my alma mater to reflect on the 'glass half-full' analogy that basically kicked off his national trajectory, my hands started shaking all over again. Thirteen years ago, I was a terrified, unpaid intern with a shaky grip and a desperate need to impress, tasked with ensuring the lectern was prepared. In my nervous haze, I didn't just fill that glass halfway as per the protocol—I filled it to the absolute, precarious brim.

I spent the next forty-five minutes of the speech watching with bated breath, convinced that the slightest vibration from the podium would cause a tidal wave that would ruin the entire political future of the country. Every time he gestured, I held my own breath, praying for surface tension to be the hero of the day. Instead, he looked at that overflowing glass and improvised a speech about optimism that resonated with millions.

Now that he is coming back to campus, I have been officially warned by the administrative staff to stay at least three hundred meters away from any beverage dispensing equipment. They call me 'The Variable' in the event planning manual, and apparently, my accidental over-pouring is still referenced as a cautionary tale in the student union's logistics handbook under the chapter titled 'Unintended Symbolic Excess.'
caption: From accidental intern to national footnote, my pouring career peaked thirteen years ago. Here's to hoping the water stays in the pitcher this time. #SRCC #PoliticalHistory #TheGlassHalfFull #CampusLife (satire)
